land.text: the metropole: Sweden, whose Africa Company (Carloff, first administrator) founded the colony on 22 April 1650

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Swedish Empire 1612-1814 is the metropole; the Dutch Gold Coast dossier (af-04-a) used swedish-empire as the counterpart of its 1656 and 1665 events, which should read swedish-gold-coast.

land.text: Fort Carlsborg at Cape Coast, 'part of the Dutch Gold Coast' from April 1663

successors.note: Formal Swedish relinquishment 22 July 1667 (infobox); the English under Robert Holmes seized the Dutch-controlled area on 9 May 1664.

capitals.name: Fort Carolusborg (Cape Coast)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Fort Carolusborg; the fort was in Danish hands from 27 January 1658 and under Dutch occupation March 1659 - December 1660. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Cape Coast point.

correction.text: Fort Carlsborg (Cape Coast), Fort William (Anomabu) and Fort Batenstein (Butri), founded 1650

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox 'Established: 22 April 1650'; 'The colony consisted of only a few forts and trading posts scattered around Cabo Corso'. The fort table gives Cape Coast (Carlsborg, 1650), Anomabu (William, 1650) and Butri near Sekondi-Takoradi (Batenstein, 1650); 12 km circles stand for the forts. No area on the page.

correction.text: adds Fort Christiansborg at Osu, Accra (1652)
Fort Carlsborg alone, under Swedish administration again from 10 December 1660

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Under Swedish administration 22 April 1650 - January/February 1658, and again 10 December 1660 - 22 April 1663.' 1658-1660 the Swedes hold no fort (Carlsborg and Christiansborg Danish in 1658, Witsen ceded 1658, then the Dutch occupation of March 1659 - December 1660), so no shape is drawn for those years.

region.text: Fort Carlsborg at Cape Coast, Fort William at Anomabu, Fort Batenstein at Butri

ledger.note: 1650 (22 April): the Swedish Gold Coast is founded at Cabo Corso. 'On 22 April 1650, the Swedish Gold Coast was founded and Carloff became its first administrator'; 'In 1652, the foundations were laid of the Fort Carlsborg'. 'Carloff made a treaty with the Akan King of Futu (also Feta) on selling some areas of land' (undated).
1652: Fort Christiansborg is built at Osu, Accra. Fort table: 'Christiansborg ... Osu, Accra ... 1652'.
1653: Fort Witsen at Sekondi-Takoradi (Taccorari). Fort table: 'Witsen ... Sekondi-Takoradi ... 1653'.
1655: Apollonia at Beyin. Fort table: 'Apollonia ... Beyin, Western Region ... 1655'.
1656: Fort Batenstein is ceded. Fort table: 'Fort Batenstein (1650, ceded 1656)' at Butri; the recipient is not named on the page (the Dutch Gold Coast dossier has the Dutch gaining it in 1656).

region.text: Fort William at Anomabu and Apollonia at Beyin

ledger.counterpart: recipient not named on the page
ledger.note: 1657: Fort William and Apollonia are lost. Fort table: William at Anomabu 'Ceded/lost 1657'; Apollonia at Beyin 1657. The page names no recipient.
1658: Fort Christiansborg is captured by the Danes. Fort table: 'Captured by the Danes in 1658'.

ledger.counterpart: recipient not named on the page
ledger.note: 1658: Fort Witsen is ceded. Fort table: 'Witsen ... ceded 1658'; the page names no recipient.

1658 (27 January): Carloff returns with a Danish privateer and takes Fort Carlsborg. 'He left Cabo Corso only to return on 27 January 1658 on the Danish Privateer Glückstadt'; 'Fort Carlsborg was seized and made part of the Danish Gold Coast colony'.

1660 (10 December): Swedish administration returns to Fort Carlsborg. 'After the Treaty of Copenhagen in 1660, Cabo Corso Castle was to be returned to Swedish administration'; a Futu-backed Swedish administration began on 10 December 1660, with the Dutch (partial occupation March 1659 - December 1660) never fully out. The Dutch are the researcher's reading of the previous holder.

1663 (April): the Dutch seize Fort Carlsborg. 'On 20 April 1663, the capital Fort Carlsborg and Fort Christiansborg were again seized by the Dutch' (History section); infobox 'Dutch capture: 22 April 1663'. 'Disappeared for good in April 1663 when it became part of the Dutch Gold Coast.'
1663 (April): the Swedish Gold Coast ends. 'Under Swedish control for eleven years, it disappeared for good in April 1663'; formal Swedish relinquishment 22 July 1667.

wars.name: Danish-Swedish struggle for Cabo Corso
wars.outcome: Carloff retook Fort Carlsborg for the Danes on 27 January 1658; Samuel Schmidt sold the colony to the Dutch West India Company in April 1659; the Dutch occupied it March 1659 - December 1660; the Treaty of Copenhagen (1660) returned Cabo Corso to Swedish administration.
wars.note: The page does not say Carlsborg stayed Danish to 1660.

wars.name: Dutch capture of the Swedish Gold Coast
wars.outcome: Dutch victory: Fort Carlsborg and Fort Christiansborg seized on 20 (infobox 22) April 1663; Sweden formally relinquished the colony on 22 July 1667; the English seized the area on 9 May 1664.

certainty.note: Forts with their grounds, drawn as circles; the page gives no boundary for any.

sources.title: Swedish Gold Coast
sources.note: Infobox dates (22 April 1650, 27 January 1658, March 1659 - December 1660, 22 April 1663, 22 July 1667), the fort table with towns and dates, Carloff, Futu treaty, Danish capture, Dutch sale and seizure, English 1664; no area.

notes: Swedish Gold Coast has no Cliopatria row; it was named a counterpart by the Danish and Dutch dossiers (af-04-a), which used swedish-empire. One page opened (opened three times for different sections; budget 1-2). The page gives no area; 12 km circles stand for each fort (towns from the fort table; Cape Coast is a gazetteer place, Anomabu, Butre, Beyin are not and are listed). Disagreements on the page: 20 April 1663 (History) vs 22 April 1663 (infobox and table); 'Fort Carolusborg' vs 'Fort Carlsborg'; the Danish capture on 27 January 1658 (History) vs 'Partial Danish capture' in the infobox; the 1663 seizure includes Christiansborg although the table has it Danish from 1658. The Danish dossier's founding at 'January/February 1658' and Christiansborg dates (1658/1659-1661) are not repeated here. Between 1658 and 1660 no shape is drawn (the Swedes held nothing); recipients of the 1657-1658 cessions are not on the page. Gazetteer names needed: Anomabu, Butre (page spells Butri), Beyin.
